title: A globally generated projective bundle is H-projective
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\mathcal E$ be a finite type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module [pqf-def-coherent] generated by finitely many global sections [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections], and let $\pi:\mathbf P_S(\mathcal E)=\operatorname{Proj}_S(\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_S}\mathcal E)	o S$ be its projective-bundle morphism [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism], using the relative Proj [def-nagata-relative-proj] of the quasi-coherent symmetric algebra [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra]. Then $\pi$ is H-projective, i.e. projective in the finite-projective-space convention [def-kun-projective].

source.place: Lemma Tag 087S (lemma-projective-over-quasi-projective-is-H-projective), proof paragraph beginning 'If $\mathcal{E}$ is generated by finitely many global sections'

proof.text: Choose a finite generating family $s_0,\ldots,s_r\in\Gamma(S,\mathcal E)$ with $r\geq0$, padding an empty family by the zero section. By [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections] its evaluation map $\varepsilon:\mathcal O_S^{\oplus(r+1)}\to\mathcal E$, $(f_i)\mapsto\sum_i f_i s_i$, is surjective as a map of sheaves. Apply [lem-trf-symmetric-sheaf-map-degreewise-surjective] to this map: it gives a degree-preserving morphism $\operatorname{Sym}(\varepsilon)$, identity in degree zero and surjective as a map of sheaves in each degree. The source is the symmetric algebra of the standard finite free sheaf.

source.place: Lemma Tag 087S, proof paragraph beginning 'If $\mathcal{E}$ is generated by finitely many global sections'

proof.text: Clause (3) of [prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality] applied to $\operatorname{Sym}(\varepsilon)$ gives a closed immersion $\iota:\mathbf P_S(\mathcal E)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Proj}_S(\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal O_S^{\oplus(r+1)}))$ over $S$. With $p$ the target's relative-Proj structural morphism [def-nagata-relative-proj], this says $\pi=p\circ\iota$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 087S, proof paragraph beginning 'If $\mathcal{E}$ is generated by finitely many global sections'

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-free-projective-bundle-base-change-space] with this $r$. It gives an isomorphism $\theta$ from the target of $\iota$ to $\mathbf P(\{0,\ldots,r\};S)$ with $q\circ\theta=p$, where $q$ is the first projection. Set $i=\theta\circ\iota$. An isomorphism preserves closed subsets and identifies the structure sheaves, so the defining closed-immersion conditions [def-weil-closed-immersion] for $\iota$ also hold for $i$. Then $q\circ i=p\circ\iota=\pi$. This is the finite-projective-space factorization of [def-kun-projective], with $N=r$, proving the claim.

source.place: Lemma Tag 087S, proof paragraph beginning 'If $\mathcal{E}$ is generated by finitely many global sections': the identification $\mathbf{P}(\mathcal{O}_S^{\oplus n}) = \mathbf{P}^{n-1}_S$
